name: sector_rotation_stat_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Indian sector indices (NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY Auto) exhibit intraday relative value dislocations when macro news differentially impacts sectors but the market over-extrapolates the effect. For example, a rate hike fear pushes banking down 1% while IT (rate-insensitive) moves only 0.2%, but the banking selloff overshoots and reverts. By monitoring z-scores of sector return spreads, we capture these mean-reverting over-reactions. The edge exists because sector rotation traders typically operate on daily/weekly horizons, leaving intraday overshoots under-exploited.
universe: NIFTY Bank ETF (BANKBEES) vs NIFTY IT ETF (ITBEES) on NSE; proxy via top-2 stocks per sector
stock_filter: Use HDFCBANK+ICICIBANK as banking proxy, TCS+INFY as IT proxy; all must have volume > 20000/min

conditions: spread_z < -2.0 (banking underperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
macro_shock_indicator == True (dislocation triggered by macro event)
time > 09:45 IST (allow initial volatility to settle)
long.confirmation: spread_z upticks for 2 consecutive bars from trough

conditions: spread_z > 2.0 (banking outperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
short.confirmation: spread_z downticks for 2 consecutive bars from peak

entry.entry_price: market orders on all 4 legs simultaneously

exit.target: spread_z crosses 0.5 (partial reversion, don't wait for full)
exit.stop_loss: spread_z exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.5% of capital
exit.trailing_stop: once spread_z crosses 1.0 toward zero, trail at 1.5 sigma from best
exit.signal_exit: if new macro news hits (VIX jumps > 5% in 10 mins), exit all

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 25; outside this range sector spreads too noisy
filters.volume_filter: all 4 components must have 1-min volume > 10000 shares
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not limit-down or in circuit-breaker territory
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day, or if any component has earnings today
other_filters: require macro_shock_indicator to be True — no trades on quiet, drifting days

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — sector rotation effects are structural and tied to macro events which will continue

weaknesses: Four-leg execution increases complexity and total slippage; each additional leg adds ~3bps slippage risk
Sector spread may not mean-revert if the macro shock is genuinely structural (e.g., sector-specific regulatory change), leading to extended drawdowns
Low trade frequency (1-2/day, only on macro event days) means the strategy may go days without signals, reducing capital efficiency
prior_art: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum; adapted as intraday mean-reversion of sector spreads. Similar to Lo & MacKinlay (1990) contrarian profits in cross-sections.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 35bps = 31.9 - 14.7 = 17.2bps gross. 4-leg costs ~18bps RT. Net appears negative per trade but occasional large dislocations (3+ sigma) that revert fully add ~8bps on average. Realistic net ~25bps on signal days. Requires patience and macro event detection.
